figures.caption: Fig. 3 | Composition analysis and structure characterization at the negative electrode/electrolyte interface. High-resolution XPS spectra of the LPSC electrolyte interface from the symmetric cells after Li plating/stripping. The Li|LPSC|Li and Li-In-S|LPSC|Li-In-S symmetric cells were disassembled after Li plating/stripping at a current density of 0.2 mA cm−2/0.2 mAh cm−2 for 100 h under 25 °C, and the Li or Li-In-S electrodes were peeled off to expose the cycled LPSC electrolyte interface for XPS measurements. a S 2p and P 2p XPS spectra of the Li/LPSC interface and b S 2p and P 2p XPS spectra of the Li-In-S/LPSC interface after Li plating/stripping collected at different sputtering times. c TOF-SIMS depth profiling results of several representative fragments for the Li/LPSC and Li-In-S/LPSC interface before and after Li plating/stripping. The symmetric cells were disassembled under the same testing conditions mentioned above, and the Li or Li-In-S electrodes were peeled off to expose the electrode interface for TOF-SIMS measurements. Raman spectroscopy detection at the d Li/LPSC and e Li-In-S/LPSC interface in the Li symmetric cell after lithiation. The symmetric cells were disassembled under different lithiation states, and the specific capacity continued to increase by 0.2 mAh cm−2. The Li or Li-In-S electrodes were peeled off to expose the LPSC electrolyte interface for Raman measurements. Top-view SEM images of f the Li and g the Li-In-S electrodes exfoliated from the symmetric cells under the same testing conditions mentioned above. AFM images and corresponding Young's modulus of h the Li and i the Li-In-S foil.
